why: Two boundary searches on the same sorted array: the first index with value >= target (bisect_left) and the first index with value > target (bisect_right). The block between them is every copy, and its size is the count of target.
hints: One binary search finds one boundary. How many boundaries does a block of equal values have?
first = first index with nums[i] >= target; last = (first index with nums[i] > target) - 1.
Write one helper 'first index where pred becomes true' and call it with two predicates, or use bisect_left / bisect_right. If first == n or nums[first] != target, return [-1, -1]. O(log n).
pitfalls: Empty array and a target bigger than every value both leave first == n.
A linear scan out from one found copy is O(n) when the whole array is the target.
constraints:
• 0 <= nums.length <= 105
  • -109 <= nums[i], target <= 109
  • nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.
  • Aim for O(log n) time.
